rationale: Merge the standalone 400 Paul Avenue Data Center record into Novva Data Centers. Novva announced that it had acquired 400 Paul on November 29, 2023 and now markets the campus solely as Novva Data Centers–San Francisco. Preserve the site's CIM/1547 acquisition, construction and pre-Novva marketing history as Novva milestones and citations, while retaining only one current manager-level CIM ownership period on Novva. The seller, exact Novva closing date, fund, ownership percentage, retained historical site economics and commissioned capacity are not publicly disclosed and are not inferred.

afterImage.name: Novva Data Centers
afterImage.description: Novva Data Centers is a CIM Group-backed U.S. wholesale and colocation data-center platform serving hyperscale, cloud, artificial-intelligence and enterprise customers across the western United States. The company was founded in 2020 with funding from CIM and Novva's founders, received an additional US$355 million of CIM growth equity in 2022 and announced US$2 billion of new financing with CIM in 2025. Novva announced on November 29, 2023 that it had acquired the 400 Paul Avenue campus in San Francisco and now markets the site as Novva Data Centers–San Francisco. The campus had been acquired by a CIM/1547 joint venture in August 2017, entered construction in April 2018 and was marketed at approximately 24 MW before Novva's acquisition; Novva currently markets 36 MW on the 7.5-acre site. The seller, exact Novva closing date, retained CIM/1547 site economics and independently verified commissioned capacity are not publicly disclosed. CIM remains the current manager-level sponsor of Novva; its fund, vehicle and ownership percentage are not public. 400 Paul is an underlying facility and alias rather than a separate PortCo. No later sale or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 23, 2026.
